title: Monitor not showing
author: thany
summary: Power Display omits an LG HDR 4K monitor even though the reporter can query a complete VCP capability set for it. The current evidence confirms DDC/CI communication but does not identify which discovery or filtering decision excluded the display.

status.label: More diagnostic context needed
status.detail: The monitor and its VCP capabilities are visible to another tool, but a fresh PowerToys diagnostic captured while Power Display omits it is needed to distinguish enumeration, connection, and filtering failures.

next_action.label: Request focused diagnostics
next_action.reason: Ask for a fresh /bugreport immediately after reproducing and the monitor connection path.

judgment.rationale: The supplied screenshot and VCP capability dump establish the symptom and DDC/CI support, but they do not show whether Power Display enumerates and rejects the monitor or never receives it from the Windows display APIs.
evidence: PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 on Windows 11 omits the LG HDR 4K monitor from Power Display.
The reporter supplied a screenshot of the missing-monitor state.
A separate VCP query identifies the display as LG HDR 4K and reports 46 VCP codes, including brightness, contrast, input source, and power mode.
No PowerToys diagnostic archive or connection topology is currently attached.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a fresh PowerToys bug report captured immediately after opening Power Display with the monitor missing, plus the physical connection path and whether Windows Settings detects the monitor.

issue_context.summary: Power Display does not list a connected LG HDR 4K display, although another utility can address the monitor and enumerate its DDC/CI VCP capabilities.
known_information: The issue reproduces with PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 installed from GitHub on Windows 11.
The reporter supplied a screenshot showing the Power Display UI without the expected monitor.
The monitor is identified as LG HDR 4K with display ID \\?\DISPLAY#GSM7706#4&311f1208&0&UID24645.
The supplied capability dump includes brightness, contrast, input source, audio, power mode, and other VCP codes.
inferences: DDC/CI communication is likely available through at least one software path because the capability query succeeded.
The failure may occur during Windows monitor enumeration, Power Display capability probing, or an internal eligibility/filtering step; the current evidence does not distinguish them.
issue_context.analysis: The VCP dump rules out a simple absence of monitor controls, but it does not contain Power Display's discovery decisions or errors. A diagnostic captured at the failure point and the connection topology would determine whether the implementation should handle a specific adapter/transport or adjust its filtering and error reporting.
initial_investigation: The issue has no assignee, duplicate link, maintainer diagnosis, or linked fix.
The reporter already supplied visual evidence and a detailed VCP capability dump, so those should not be requested again.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic archive captured while the monitor is missing from Power Display.
information_gaps.why_needed: The logs can show whether the monitor was enumerated, rejected during capability probing, or omitted before Power Display processed it.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Open Power Display, reproduce the missing-monitor state, then immediately comment /bugreport and attach the generated ZIP.

information_gaps.information: The physical connection path and Windows detection state.
information_gaps.why_needed: Direct HDMI/DisplayPort, USB-C, docks, adapters, DisplayLink, and remote/virtual paths expose different monitor APIs and can explain why VCP access succeeds in one tool but not Power Display.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: State how the LG monitor is connected, including any dock or adapter, and whether it appears normally under Windows Settings > System > Display.

comment.body: Thanks for the screenshot and the detailed VCP capability dump. That confirms the LG display exposes DDC/CI controls, but it does not show whether Power Display enumerates the monitor and filters it out or never receives it from Windows. Please open Power Display with the monitor missing, then immediately submit a comment containing `/bugreport` and attach the generated ZIP. Also tell us how the monitor is connected (direct HDMI/DisplayPort/USB-C, or through a dock/adapter/DisplayLink device) and whether it appears normally in Windows Settings > System > Display.
